subject: general
question: **A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech**. The botanist sighed that the rare orchid had germinated, only to succumb to a latent fungal blight.

options.text: The botanist sighed, "The rare orchid did germinate, only to succumb to a latent fungal blight."
The botanist sighed, "A rare orchid had germinated only to succumb to a latent fungal blight."
The botanist sighed, "The rare orchid germinated, only to succumb to a latent fungal blight."
The botanist sighed, "Rare orchid germinates but succumbs to fungus."

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Indirect Speech:** The botanist sighed that the rare orchid had germinated, only to succumb to a latent fungal blight.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"had germinated" becomes "germinated"**
 
 
• When the reporting verb is in the past tense ("sighed"), the **Past Perfect** in indirect speech usually reverts to the Simple Past<
